253	**[Section 6 --- Invoice Format and Submission Requirements]{.underline}**
254	
255	**6.1 Invoice Frequency.** Monthly invoices, submitted within thirty (30) days after the end of the billing period (e.g., invoices for May services are due by June 30).
256	
257	**6.2 Electronic Submission.** All invoices must be submitted electronically via Pinnacle\'s designated e-billing platform (currently BillingBridge™). Paper invoices will not be accepted except with prior written approval from the Relationship Attorney.
258	
259	**6.3 Invoice Format.** Each invoice shall include: Firm name and address; Pinnacle matter name and matter number; invoice number and date; billing period; itemized professional fees by timekeeper (name, title, rate, hours, amount); itemized disbursements with line numbers, dates, descriptions, quantities (where applicable), unit costs, and amounts; summary totals for professional fees and disbursements; and running total of fees and disbursements billed to date.
260	
261	**6.4 Matter Number.** All invoices must reference Pinnacle\'s internal matter number as well as the Firm\'s client/matter number.
262	
263	**6.5 Narrative Descriptions.** All entries must include narrative descriptions sufficient to permit evaluation. See Sections 4.4 and 5.1.
264	
265	**6.6 Supporting Documentation.** Vendor invoices, receipts, and supporting documentation for disbursements must be attached or made available within five (5) business days of request.
266	
267	**6.7 Accuracy.** The Firm is responsible for the mathematical accuracy of all invoices. Pinnacle will verify all calculations, and any discrepancies will be brought to the Firm\'s attention for correction. Invoice totals must accurately reflect the sum of all individual line items.
268	
269	**[Section 7 --- UTBMS Coding Requirements]{.underline}**
270	
271	**7.1** Pinnacle requires all time entries and expense entries to be coded using the Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) codes adopted by Pinnacle.
272	
273	**7.2** Each time entry must include a UTBMS task code and activity code. Each expense entry must include a UTBMS expense code. The applicable codes are set forth in Appendix C.
274	
275	**7.3** If a particular charge does not map clearly to an existing code, the Firm should contact the Relationship Attorney for guidance before submission.
276	
277	**7.4** Invoices that do not include UTBMS codes may be returned for revision and re-submission, which may delay payment.
278	
279	**[Section 8 --- Invoice Review, Dispute Resolution, and Payment Terms]{.underline}**
280	
281	**8.1 Invoice Review.** The Relationship Attorney (or designee) will review each invoice for compliance with these Guidelines and the applicable engagement letter. Pinnacle reserves the right to reduce or reject any charge that does not comply with these Guidelines, the engagement letter, or any applicable Pre-Approval.
282	
283	**8.2 Reduction Authority.**
284	
285	> \(a\) The Relationship Attorney may reduce or reject non-compliant charges without prior consultation with the Firm for reductions totaling less than Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$25,000.00) per invoice.
286	>
287	> \(b\) Reductions totaling Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$25,000.00) or more per invoice require approval from the General Counsel.
288	
289	**8.3 Notification of Reductions.** If Pinnacle reduces or rejects charges on an invoice, the Relationship Attorney will notify the billing partner of the reduction and the reason(s) within fifteen (15) business days of invoice receipt. Notification may be provided via the e-billing platform, email, or letter.
290	
291	**8.4 Disputes.** If the Firm disagrees with a reduction, it may submit a written explanation to the Relationship Attorney within fifteen (15) business days of receiving notice of the reduction. The Relationship Attorney will review the explanation and issue a final determination within fifteen (15) business days thereafter. Appeals of the Relationship Attorney\'s determination may be directed to the General Counsel, whose decision shall be final and binding.
292	
293	**8.5 Payment Terms.** Approved invoices will be paid within forty-five (45) days of receipt of a compliant invoice. Payment of disputed amounts will be held pending resolution of the dispute in accordance with this Section.
294	
295	**8.6 Retroactive Approval.** Where a charge requires Pre-Approval that was not obtained, the Firm may request retroactive approval from the Relationship Attorney (or the General Counsel, where applicable). Retroactive approval is discretionary and is not guaranteed. Granting retroactive approval in one instance does not waive the Pre-Approval requirement for future charges. Pending a decision on retroactive approval, the charge will be held and not paid.
296	
297	**[Section 9 --- Amendments, Waivers, and Effective Date]{.underline}**
298	
299	**9.1 Amendments.** These Guidelines may be amended by Pinnacle at any time. Amendments will be communicated in writing to all Outside Counsel and are effective as of the date specified in the written notice. The Firm\'s continued performance of services after the effective date of any amendment constitutes acceptance of the amended Guidelines.

A waiver with respect to one invoice, Matter, or Firm shall not constitute a waiver with respect to any other invoice, Matter, or Firm. The failure by Pinnacle to enforce any provision of these Guidelines in a particular instance shall not constitute a waiver of such provision or of Pinnacle\'s right to enforce the provision in any other instance.

304

327	**[2. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**
328	
329	HWK is engaged to represent Pinnacle in the defense of Morales v. Pinnacle Health Systems, Inc., Case No. 3:24-cv-01847-RJC, filed in the United States District Court for the Western District of North Carolina and assigned to the Honorable Robert J. Conrath Jr.
330	
331	The Morales Litigation is an employment discrimination class action brought by a putative class of approximately 312 current and former female physicians employed by Pinnacle at its hospital facilities and affiliated medical practices across the Carolinas and Virginia. The named plaintiff, Dr. Maria Elena Morales, along with three additional named plaintiffs, allege systemic gender-based pay discrimination in violation of Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as amended, 42 U.S.C. § 2000e *et seq.*, and the Equal Pay Act of 1963, 29 U.S.C. § 206(d). Plaintiffs are represented by Ostrander & Fitch, P.C. The complaint seeks compensatory damages, back pay, front pay, liquidated damages, injunctive and declaratory relief, and an award of attorneys\' fees and costs.

(4,"Hotel, J. Palermo, The Whitmore, San Francisco, 2 nights @ $319",638.00,88.00,"Reduce","Same as Line 3: $44/night over the Tier 1 cap x 2 nights.","GL §5.2; App. A; Log Entry 5"),
(5,"Dinner, M. Beale and J. Palermo, San Francisco, 5/2",214.00,64.00,"Reduce","$107 per person exceeds the $75 per-person, per-day travel meal cap (inclusive of tips). (6,"Meals, M. Beale, San Francisco, 5/3",82.00,7.00,"Reduce","Exceeds $75/day travel meal cap by $7. Description does not identify meals/vendor.","GL §5.2 (Meals During Travel)"),

(8,"Rideshare, M. Beale, SFO–hotel and return",94.50,0,"Hold","Ground transportation is reimbursable at reasonable actual cost. Both travelers flew the same itinerary and stayed at the same hotel, yet billed separate round-trip rideshares; the single 5/4 date does not match the 5/2 arrival. Request receipts. Allow one shared fare if both rode together.","GL §5.2 (Ground Transportation; General Principle – most cost-effective option); §5.1 (Description: dates)"),
(9,"Rideshare, J. Palermo, SFO–hotel and return",87.00,0,"Hold","Duplicate of Line 8 route for co-traveler. Recommend disallowance ($87.00) unless receipts show separate travel was necessary.","GL §5.2; §5.1"),

(11,"Airfare, C. Aldridge, CLT–Washington D.C. (mediator meeting)",412.00,0,"Compliant","Routine travel; below $5,000 notice threshold. Fare class not stated; confirm coach with receipt.","GL §5.2 (Air Travel; Travel Pre-Approval)"),
(12,"Hotel, C. Aldridge, The Capital Greystone, Washington D.C., 1 night",348.00,73.00,"Reduce","Washington, D.C. is a Tier 1 City ($275/night cap). Excess of $73 not pre-approved.","GL §5.2 (Hotels); App. A"),
(13,"Meals, C. Aldridge, Washington D.C., 5/13",96.00,21.00,"Reduce","Exceeds $75/day travel meal cap by $21. Description lacks meal/vendor and purpose.","GL §5.2 (Meals During Travel); §5.1"),
(14,"Rental car, M. Beale, Greenville SC, full-size sedan, 1 day",127.00,127.00,"Reject","Full-size sedans are expressly not reimbursable. No documentation that a mid-size vehicle was unavailable. (15,"Internal photocopies, 12,400 pages @ $0.15",1860.00,620.00,"Reduce","B&W internal copying is capped at $0.10/page and “shall not be exceeded.” Overcharge of $0.05 x 12,400 = $620. (16,"Color copies, 840 pages @ $0.25",210.00,0,"Compliant","Rate matches $0.25/page cap. Description lacks purpose; request supplementation.","GL §5.3 (Color Copies); §5.1 (Descriptions)"),
(17,"Outside printing, trial exhibit binders, Copyland Express",3475.00,0,"Hold","Outside vendor printing is reimbursable at actual cost with vendor invoice. Trial is not set until February 2026 and the case is at class certification/mediation stage; HWK must explain necessity of trial exhibit binders in May 2025 and produce the Copyland invoice. Below $5,000, so no pre-approval required.","GL §5.3 (Outside Printing); §5.1 (Documentation; Descriptions); §6.6"),
(18,"Outside printing, class cert brief and appendices, Copyland Express",2180.00,0,"Hold","Brief was filed and served via CM/ECF (Fee Lines 56–57). Request Copyland invoice and explanation (e.g., courtesy copies required by chambers). Combined Copyland charges in May total $5,655.","GL §5.3; §5.1; §6.6"),
(19,"Scanning/OCR, legacy personnel files, 34,000 pp, DataScan Solutions",6800.00,6800.00,"Reject","Single line item exceeds $5,000; scanning charges over $5,000 are expressly subject to pre-approval. No pre-approval for DataScan appears in the certified log. Charge may be rejected in full; any retroactive approval is discretionary and the charge is held unpaid pending decision.","GL §5.1 (Pre-Approval for Large Disbursements); §5.3 (Scanning and OCR); §8.6; EL §6"),
(20,"Binding and tab sets, mediation binders, 12 sets @ $30",360.00,0,"Compliant","Litigation binding reimbursable at actual cost. Vendor not identified and 12 sets appears generous for a mediation; request backup confirming actual cost (not internal supplies, which are overhead).","GL §5.3 (Binding); §5.1 (Overhead)"),
(21,"Color copies, demonstratives, 220 pp @ $0.25",55.00,0,"Compliant","Rate and description compliant.","GL §5.3"),
(22,"Dr. Evelyn Hartsfield, May invoice",32500.00,0,"Compliant","Pre-approved expert; GC concurrence obtained for monthly fees up to $35,000 cap. On its own, within cap — but see Line 27. Original expert invoice must be attached.","GL §5.4; Log Entry 2"),
(23,"Redmond Consulting Group, May invoice",18750.00,0,"Compliant","Pre-approved consultant; within $20,000 monthly cap and below $25,000 GC threshold. Original invoice must be attached.","GL §5.4; Log Entry 3"),
(24,"Dr. Leonard Voss, vocational rehabilitation expert",4200.00,4200.00,"Reject","Every expert/consultant engagement requires written pre-approval BEFORE retention regardless of cost. Dr. Voss does not appear in the certified pre-approval log. Vocational experts are expressly within the scope of §5.4.","GL §5.4 (Pre-Approval Required; Scope); EL §§2, 6(d); Log Certification"),
(25,"GraphicWorks LLC, litigation graphics and demonstratives",7850.00,7850.00,"Reject","Graphics/demonstrative vendors providing substantive consulting services are “consultants” requiring pre-approval; the charge also exceeds the $5,000 single-line threshold. No pre-approval in the log under either provision.","GL §5.4 (Scope of Consultants); §5.1 (Pre-Approval > $5,000); Log Certification"),
(26,"TechForensic Partners, ESI forensic imaging, 3 devices",5100.00,0,"Compliant","Pre-approved 5/18/25 at approx. $5,100; billed amount matches. Vendor invoice must be attached; chain-of-custody documentation to be maintained.","GL §5.1; Log Entry 6"),
(27,"Dr. Evelyn Hartsfield, additional rush analysis",8400.00,5900.00,"Reduce","Combined Hartsfield May charges are $40,900 (Lines 22 + 27), exceeding the $35,000 approved monthly cap by $5,900. Overage required advance GC authorization; none is in the log. The rush work was ordered “per Aldridge request” without notice to the Relationship Attorney. Separately, $8,400 is not a multiple of the approved $650 rate (12.92 hrs), suggesting an unapproved rush premium — obtain original invoice.","GL §5.4 (Budget Caps; Monthly Threshold); Log Entry 2; EL §§6(d), 7"),
(28,"Filing fee, motion to compel",52.00,0,"Hold","Federal district courts generally do not charge a fee to file a motion via CM/ECF, and the motion was filed 5/6 (Fee Line 15), not 5/5. Request court receipt before payment.","GL §5.5 (documentation on request); §6.6"),
(29,"Certified copy of court order",24.00,0,"Compliant","Routine court cost at actual cost.","GL §5.5"),
(30,"Pro hac vice fee, T. Nakamura, WDNC",250.00,0,"Compliant","Pro hac vice admission fees are expressly reimbursable court costs; Nakamura’s possible pro hac vice admission was contemplated in EL §3.","GL §5.5; EL §3"),
(31,"Service of subpoena, Dr. Helen Kuroda",185.00,0,"Compliant","Service of process fee reimbursable. Note: Kuroda was already deposed 5/3 and is a class member; Relationship Attorney may wish to confirm purpose.","GL §5.5"),
(32,"FedEx overnight, class certification motion to court",32.50,0,"Hold","Description fails to identify origin/destination and the reason overnight delivery was required; filings in this case are made via CM/ECF and the class certification motion is plaintiffs’ (HWK filed its opposition 5/23). Return for revision.","GL §5.6 (Overnight; Descriptions)"),
(33,"FedEx overnight, privilege log to opposing counsel",28.75,0,"Hold","No reason given for overnight rather than electronic service; origin/destination not stated. Return for revision.","GL §5.6"),
(34,"Courier, Charlotte, mediation materials to Judge Royce’s office",45.00,0,"Hold","Mediator Royce met with C. Aldridge in Washington, D.C. on 5/12 — the same day — yet a local Charlotte courier is billed to her office. Origin, destination and reason not stated. Return for revision.","GL §5.6 (Local Courier; Descriptions)"),
(35,"FedEx overnight, expert report to opposing counsel",34.25,0,"Hold","Expert report not identified; no reason for overnight vs. electronic service; addresses not stated. Return for revision.","GL §5.6"),
(36,"FedEx overnight, office supplies to HWK Charlotte office",18.50,18.50,"Reject","Shipping of firm office supplies is overhead and expressly non-reimbursable.","GL §5.6 (Non-Reimbursable Deliveries); §5.1 (Overhead)"),
(37,"Working lunch, M. Beale and D. Yamashita, Heirloom Bistro",118.00,18.00,"Reduce","Qualifying meal (Pinnacle personnel present) but working-lunch cap is $50/person inclusive of tax and tip; 2 x $50 = $100 allowable. Confirm no alcohol.","GL §5.7 (Per-Person Caps; Alcohol)"),
(38,"Working dinner, Aldridge, Beale, Palermo + two summer associates, Carmichael’s Steakhouse",612.00,612.00,"Reject","Attended solely by Firm personnel — not reimbursable regardless of work discussed. Summer associate involvement is non-billable professional development. Even if it qualified, $122.40/person exceeds the $85 dinner cap.","GL §5.7 (Working Meals); §3.5"),
(39,"Working lunch, M. Beale, solo at desk",24.00,24.00,"Reject","Solo meal by Firm personnel; no Pinnacle personnel or third-party witness present. Overhead.","GL §5.7 (Working Meals)"),
(40,"Working dinner, Aldridge and Beale with plaintiff’s counsel, The Piedmont Room",247.00,247.00,"Reject","Opposing counsel is neither Pinnacle personnel nor a third-party witness or party; meal does not fall within either permitted attendee category. Description also omits names/titles of plaintiff’s counsel attendees and per-person cost; alcohol not addressed. If the Relationship Attorney elects to treat it as a working meal, cap at $85/attendee after alcohol deduction upon a compliant resubmission.","GL §5.7 (Working Meals; Client Entertainment; Descriptions; Alcohol)"),
(41,"Relativity hosting, 2.4 TB, May",14200.00,2200.00,"Reduce","Approved monthly budget is “not to exceed $12,000” (11/12/24). No re-authorization was sought although data grew from 1.8 TB to 2.4 TB. Excess of $2,200 rejected per the approval’s own terms.","GL §5.8(a)–(b); Log Entry 1; EL §6(e)"),
(42,"Westlaw research charges",3870.00,3870.00,"Reject","Legal research databases are overhead and not separately billable under any allocation method; E106 charges are automatically rejected.","GL §5.1 (Overhead); §5.8 (Legal Research Databases); App. C (E106); EL §6(g)"),
(43,"Video conferencing platform license",125.00,125.00,"Reject","Routine video conferencing platform licenses are overhead; no case-specific service (e.g., remote deposition platform) is identified.","GL §5.8 (Video Conferencing)"),
(44,"Data analytics software, predictive coding module, monthly",2200.00,2200.00,"Reject","Predictive coding/TAR is an e-discovery processing cost under §5.8(a), and HWK’s Relativity request itself described predictive coding as within the approved platform scope. May e-discovery spend is $16,400 (Lines 41 + 44) against the $12,000 cap; this line falls entirely above the cap without re-authorization.","GL §5.8(a)–(b); Log Entry 1"),
(45,"Contract attorney R. Chen, 142 hrs @ $75",10650.00,1420.00,"Reduce","Chen approved only at $65/hr; the requested $75 exception was expressly denied (4/22/25). $65 cap has no exception absent GC written approval. Excess $10 x 142 hrs = $1,420; allowable $9,230.","GL §5.9 (Rate Cap; No Markup); Log Entry 4; EL §§4, 6(f)"),
(46,"Contract attorney S. Mehta, 168 hrs @ $65",10920.00,0,"Compliant","Pre-approved at $65/hr. Confirm rate equals amount actually paid to agency (no markup).","GL §5.9; Log Entry 4"),
(47,"Contract attorney A. Brooks, privilege review, 96 hrs @ $65",6240.00,6240.00,"Reject","Each contract attorney must be individually pre-approved; approval of Chen and Mehta does not extend to Brooks. No approval for Brooks in the certified log. Privilege review also approaches substantive work that EL §3 bars delegating to contract attorneys without written consent.","GL §5.9 (Pre-Approval Required); EL §3; Log Certification"),
]

python3 -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,\"/workspace/work\"); from lines import L
b=sum(x[2] for x in L); r=sum(x[3] for x in L)
print(len(L), round(b,2), round(r,2), round(b-r,2))
from collections import Counter; print(Counter(x[4] for x in L))
print(round(sum(x[2] for x in L if x[4]==\"Hold\"),2))
"'

Jan. 15, 2024 ("GL"); (3) Pre-Approval Correspondence Log, certified by D. Yamashita June 5, 2025 ("Log"); (4) HWK Engagement Letter dated Oct. 1, 2024, countersigned Oct. 3, 2024 ("EL")
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# I. Executive Summary

All 47 disbursement line items on the May 2025 invoice were tested against the Guidelines, the six certified pre-approvals in the Log, and the disbursement terms of the Engagement Letter (which incorporates the Guidelines and provides that the more restrictive provision controls; GL §1, EL §6). The principal conclusions are:

- **Invoice cannot be paid as submitted.** The disbursement schedule does not foot. The 47 line items total \$145,404.30, but the invoice Summary and the schedule's own "TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS" line state \$86,742.19 --- a \$58,662.11 discrepancy. The professional-fee schedule is also misstated in the opposite direction (line items total \$161,698.50 vs. \$187,420.00 stated). The invoice violates GL §6.7 and should be returned for correction before any payment.

- **Recommended reductions: \$42,822.30.** Recommended reductions total \$42,822.30 across 24 line items (11 reduced, 13 rejected in full), leaving \$102,582.00 in allowable disbursements measured against the line items.

- **Items on hold: \$6,029.00.** A further 9 line items totaling \$6,029.00 should be held pending supporting documentation or revised descriptions (Part V). One of these (Line 9, \$87.00) is likely to become a reduction.

- **GC approval required.** Because the reductions exceed \$25,000 for this invoice, they require General Counsel approval before being imposed (GL §8.2(b); EL §5). Notice of reductions is due to the billing partner within 15 business days of receipt (GL §8.3).

- **Root cause: pre-approval discipline.** Approximately 86% of the dollar value of the reductions (\$36,810.00) stems from unapproved or over-cap third-party spend: an unapproved expert (Dr. Voss), an unapproved consultant (GraphicWorks), an unapproved contract attorney (A.
